title: October 2026 Crypto Card Volume Report: RedotPay, ether.fi & KAST Lead a $1.37B Month
seoTitle: Top Crypto Cards by Volume (October 2026): $1.37B Leaderboard
excerpt: Crypto card settlement volume hit $1.37B in October 2026, up 11.3% month over month. See the top 10 programs ranked by volume, ARR and market share - led by RedotPay, ether.fi and KAST.

mainImage.alt: Three glass payment cards on an ascending podium with coins flowing upward - the October 2026 crypto card volume leaderboard led by RedotPay, ether.fi and KAST

keyTakeaways: Crypto card settlement volume reached $1.37 billion in October 2026, up 11.3% month over month, pushing 44-month cumulative throughput to $13.87 billion across 32 tracked programs.
363.3K active wallets executed 12.94 million card swipes - roughly 35.6 swipes per spender and a ~$105.87 average ticket, or about $3,771 of monthly spend per active wallet.

Three programs cleared the $82.2M/month threshold for the $1B+ annualized run-rate club: RedotPay ($423.5M, 30.9% share), ether.fi Cash ($141.9M, 10.4%) and KAST ($121.0M, 8.8%) - 50.1% of the market combined.

Custodial programs like RedotPay book volume at the deposit boundary, while self-custodial cards like ether.fi Cash, Tria and COCA settle swipe-by-swipe on-chain - so raw rankings mix two different accounting methods.
Volume is not value: #1 RedotPay scores 5.5-6.5/10 on fee drag, while higher-rated challengers like Bleap (8.0), Plasma One (7.8) and ether.fi Cash (7.6) pair scale with better net returns.

children.text: Macro market acceleration: from the GENIUS Act ($339.7M) to $1.37 billion per month

The 44-month curve from March 2023 to October 2026 has a clear inflection point: the passage of the GENIUS Act in July 2025, when monthly sector volume sat at $339.7 million. Regulatory clarity turned stablecoin payment rails into an institutional and consumer product almost overnight. Within exactly one year, July 2026 delivered the first $1B+ month at $1.04 billion - and three months later October printed $1.37 billion, a further +31.7% expansion with +11.3% month-over-month velocity.

Methodology note: why custodial top-up volume differs from self-custodial swipe settlement
is easy to miss but changes how you should read every rank: total volume alone cannot rank cards fairly, because custodial programs book deposits while

settle swipe-by-swipe on-chain. When a user moves $5,000 of USDT into a custodial prepaid card like RedotPay or KAST, that inflow is recorded at the funding boundary - whether or not it is ever spent. When the same $5,000 sits in a self-custodial card like ether.fi Cash, Plasma One, Tria or COCA, it stays in the user's own smart contract until the exact millisecond a merchant terminal requests it. Every dollar of self-custodial volume is therefore verified point-of-sale settlement, while custodial volume is partially a deposit float measure. faqs.question: Which crypto card has the highest transaction volume in 2026?
faqs.answer: In October 2026, RedotPay ranked #1 globally with $423.5 million in monthly volume (a $5.15 billion annualized run-rate), capturing 30.9% of the $1.37 billion crypto card market, followed by ether.fi Cash ($141.9M; 10.4% share) and KAST ($121.0M; 8.8% share).

faqs.question: How big is the global crypto card market in October 2026?
faqs.answer: Across the 32 stablecoin card programs tracked by Rituel via Paymentscan and WaldenPay settlement data, monthly volume reached $1.37 billion in October 2026 (+11.3% month over month), bringing 44-month cumulative volume since March 2023 to $13.87 billion across 363.3K active wallets and 12.94 million monthly card swipes.

faqs.question: What is the $1B Annualized Run-Rate (ARR) Club on the Rituel Leaderboard?
faqs.answer: The $1B ARR Club represents crypto card programs processing at least $82.2 million in monthly settlement volume (monthly volume x 365/30 >= $1B). As of October 2026 only three programs qualify: RedotPay ($5.15B ARR), ether.fi Cash (~$1.73B ARR) and KAST (~$1.47B ARR).

faqs.question: Why do custodial and self-custodial crypto cards report volume differently?
faqs.answer: Custodial programs like RedotPay and KAST book volume when users deposit stablecoins into the issuer's funding wallets, whereas self-custodial cards like ether.fi Cash, Plasma One, Tria and COCA keep funds in user-controlled smart contracts and record volume swipe-by-swipe as merchant transactions settle on-chain.
